name: Plainlimit: Screen Time Limit
subtitle: Your essentials never count
promotional_text: Pick your essentials, like calls, texts and maps: they never touch your battery. Everything else drains six cells a day, and when it’s empty you earn time back with sums.
description:
Plainlimit is a screen time limit that leaves your essentials alone.

You pick your essentials: calls, texts, maps, or any other app you use as a tool. They never count and never lock, because using your phone as a tool shouldn't cost you anything. Everything else runs on a battery: set a daily goal, and the apps that count drain six cells as you use them.

When the battery is empty, those apps lock, with friction rather than a wall: solve 3 sums for 15 more minutes, then 5 for 10, then 7 for 5, and 3 more sums each time after that until it recharges. Just enough that picking the phone back up is a choice, while your essentials stay open.

- Any app can be an essential: tick the ones your phone is for in Apple's list, and everything else counts
- It recharges at 6:00 AM, or a time you choose, not at midnight, so there is no fresh battery for a late-night scroll
- Settings lock while the battery is empty, so the goal can't be raised halfway through a scroll
- A battery you can read at a glance, on the Today screen and in a Home Screen widget
- A warning screen on your last cell, so the lock never comes as a surprise
- Second thought: a pause before the apps you open without thinking. Pick them, and each asks for one sum before it opens
- Choose how firm an empty battery is: a red screen you can tap through, sums for a little more time, or locked until it recharges
- Your last seven days, and the apps that used the most today, drawn by Apple's Screen Time
- Tips for using your phone less, with where to find each setting

Plainlimit counts and locks with Apple's Screen Time, on your iPhone. It never sees which apps you open: it is only told how much of your day has gone. There is no account, no server, no analytics and no ads.

Apps that iOS keeps open in its Always Allowed list, such as Phone and Messages, are never locked by any app, Plainlimit included.

Plainlimit is free: the battery, your essentials, sums, the recharge and emergency passes never cost anything. Plainlimit Pro is one payment, with no subscription, for a few extras: choosing your recharge time, easy or hard sums, a large widget with your streak and passes, and a lock message in your own words.

support._about: This app's section on the apps' support page (tools/site_pages.py). Every answer must match what the app shows.
support.backup: There is nothing to back up. Plainlimit keeps only your goal, your recharge time and your last seven days, on this iPhone. On a new iPhone, install it and go through setup again: it takes about a minute.

more.q: Why didn't an app lock when the battery was empty?
more.a: Check that it isn't one of your essentials: open Settings, then Essentials. Essentials never count and never lock, and everything else does. Apps in the iPhone's Always Allowed list (Phone, Messages, FaceTime and Maps unless you changed it, in the Settings app under Screen Time) are never locked by any app.

more.q: Why is Plainlimit's figure different from Screen Time's?
more.a: Plainlimit counts every app except your essentials, from the time it recharges (6:00 AM unless you changed it). Screen Time's daily total counts every app from midnight. Use after midnight but before the recharge belongs to the day before. With Plainlimit Pro you can set the recharge to 12:00 AM in Settings, under Recharge time, to match Screen Time's day.

more.q: How do I change my essentials?
more.a: Open Settings, tap Essentials, then Choose essentials. You can have up to 50. It can't be changed while the battery is empty, so an app can't be made an essential to get around the lock; it opens again when the battery recharges.

more.q: How do I stop using it?
more.a: Delete the app. That removes everything it kept and every lock it set.

more.q: What does the free version include?
more.a: Everything that makes Plainlimit work: the battery and its lock, your essentials, sums for more time, the recharge at 6:00 AM, the settings lock and emergency passes. Plainlimit Pro is one payment for choosing your recharge time, easy or hard sums, the large widget and a lock message in your own words. A recharge time chosen before Pro existed stays as it was.

support.restore: Open the Settings tab and tap Plainlimit Pro: Restore purchase is on that screen, under Unlock Pro.

privacy_label.note: For App Store Connect > App Privacy: 'Data Not Collected'. No account, no server, no analytics, no ads and no purchase service: Pro is bought straight from the App Store (StoreKit), so nothing is collected by the developer or a third party. Apple's own handling of a purchase is Apple's, and is not declared here. Screen Time data stays in Apple's own frameworks on the device: the app gets threshold events (how much time has gone in the picked apps) and opaque app tokens, and the per-app list is drawn by Apple's report extension, which cannot send anything out.
privacy_label.everything_else: Not collected. The goal, the recharge time, the picks and the last seven days never leave the device.

review_notes:
Plainlimit is a daily screen time limit that a person sets for themselves on their own iPhone (Family Controls with individual authorization, not parental controls). There is no account and no sign-in, and the app makes no network calls of its own. One optional in-app purchase, Plainlimit Pro (non-consumable), is bought straight from the App Store: open the Settings tab and tap Plainlimit Pro. Restore purchase is on the same screen.

To try it:
1. Open the app and tap Set it up. On the Screen Time screen tap Allow, then Continue on Apple's sheet.
2. On Your essentials, tap Choose essentials. Apple's list opens twice: the first time tap All Apps & Categories at the top and tap Done; the second time tick one or two apps that should stay open (or none) and tap Done. Setup then moves on by itself.
3. On Notifications need to be on, tap Allow notifications, then Allow on Apple's sheet (the notification is how the sums are reached from a locked app in step 5).
4. On the goal screen, tap the minus button until the goal reads 0:30 (the shortest), then Next, then Start counting.
5. Use any app that is not an essential. At a 30-minute goal each of the six cells is 5 minutes. After 25 minutes the orange Last cell screen covers the app (Keep going closes it). After 30 minutes the battery is empty and the app shows Battery's empty. With the default setting, Work for it, its I need more time button sends a notification that opens Plainlimit to three sums, which give 15 more minutes (apps can't be opened from that screen directly).
6. In Plainlimit's Settings tab: Daily goal, Essentials, When the battery is empty (Warn, Work for it, or Locked), and a Do more card with Second thought (picked apps ask for one sum before they open), Lock message, Sums and Recharge time (the battery refills at that time each day; changing it is part of Plainlimit Pro). Settings and Essentials are locked while the battery is empty, so an app can't be made an essential to get around the lock.

Screen Time data: Plainlimit gets only DeviceActivity threshold events (how much time has gone in the picked apps) and Apple's opaque app tokens; it never learns which apps were used. The day's total and the What used it list on the Today screen are drawn by Apple's DeviceActivityReport extension, which Plainlimit cannot read. Notifications are local only: Nearly out, and the one that opens the sums from the empty screen. The Home Screen widget shows the battery.

Apps in iOS's Always Allowed list (Phone, Messages, FaceTime and Maps by default) are never covered, as iOS requires.
